title: fix(plugins): preserve native Windows SDK filenames
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes SDK aliases returning slash-normalized filenames instead of native Windows filenames when plugins call `require.resolve()` under Bun.

## User Impact

Plugin authors get platform-native SDK filenames from native resolution while Jiti keeps its existing alias-map representation. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native resolver was returning Jiti's Windows alias spelling directly. Normalize the filename at that adapter boundary, where native resolution owns the result. The regression checks both representations and real `require.resolve()` behavior. Production code remains the same size.

The executable Commander fixtures now release their uncached plugin registries through the CLI invocation owner after command parsing. Those registries retain captured source files and SQLite ownership tokens that must close before Windows fixture deletion. The explicit session case keeps its caller-owned path, asserts that it has no executable invocation resources, and disposes its actual raw registry after the original retention assertions. All six registration cases remain intact.

## Evidence

Both complete resolver test files pass all 41 cases on the exact head `d0ba8acbbd7a03b2128fcebc7d7d6bdcd6199eb8`:

| Platform/runtime | Result | Wrapper wall time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native Windows x64, Node 24 | 41 passed | 82.135s |
| Native Windows x64, OpenClaw Bun fork | 41 passed | 75.974s |
| macOS, Node 24 | 41 passed | 27.62s |
| macOS, pinned OpenClaw Bun fork | 41 passed | 39.12s |

Windows runs had no failures, skips or timeouts, and tracked source was verified before and after. The Windows regression-only baseline failed the new native-adapter case on both runtimes and the two existing exact-filename assertions on Bun. Final proof also covers the five previously failing fixture teardowns.

The changed file alone passes 25 cases in 73.71s with `pnpm test src/plugins/loader.lazy-alias.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`; shared-host measurements are not a performance comparison. Independent local and branch P2 reviews are clean. Changed-file validation passes, including production/test type graphs, three dead-export scans, lint and guards; the runtime import-cycle check reports zero cycles.

[Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37256581223) passed on its first actual run, including all 16 selected Node test jobs (94–214 seconds each) and the required CI gate. The hosted Windows lane was skipped; Windows proof comes from the native runs above. [ClawSweeper's exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165282#issuecomment-5987248108) completed with no findings or pre-merge requests. No CI rerun or admin exception was needed.
